text: Gandalf visits Bilbo at Bag End.
The Unexpected Party.
Never quite remembering how it happened, Bilbo sets out from Bag End with Thorin and Company, bound for the Lonely Mountain.
Three trolls capture the Company; Gandalf outwits them, spurring an argument until sunrise turns them to stone.
The Company arrives in Rivendell, the Last Homely House west of the Mountains.
The Company takes a short rest in Rivendell, while the Elves sing 'O! Tra-la-la-lally'.
Midsummer's Eve. Elrond reads the moon-letters on Thrór's map, revealing the secret entrance to the Lonely Mountain.
The Company departs Rivendell the day after Elrond fortuitously discovers the moon-letters on Thrór's map.
The Company is captured by Goblins.
Gandalf kills the Great Goblin and the Dwarves escape. Bilbo finds the One Ring, exchanges riddles with Gollum, and escapes.
The Company, trapped by Wargs and Goblins, is rescued by the Eagles.
The Eagles carry the Company to the Carrock; they seek Beorn's hospitality.
Beorn, delighted at the death of the Great Goblin, lends the Company ponies for the journey to Mirkwood.
Gandalf leaves the Company at Mirkwood's edge to evict Sauron. They enter Mirkwood on foot.
They cross the Enchanted River. Bombur falls in.
The Company strays from the path, lured by lights in the forest.
Giant spiders capture the Dwarves; Bilbo rescues them.
Wood-elves capture the Company and imprison them.
Barrels Out of Bond. The Company escapes down the Forest River.
The Company arrives in Lake-town on Bilbo's birthday.
The Company receives a warm welcome in Lake-town.
The Company rows north from Lake-town.
They leave the boats and cross the Desolation of the Dragon.
The Company set up camp in the western valley.
On the Doorstep. Bilbo finds the hidden path to the secret door.
The last light of Durin's Day. The thrush knocks; the secret door opens. Bilbo descends alone to speak with Smaug.
Bilbo returns to Smaug's lair. Roused to fury, the dragon scorches Lake-town and is slain by Bard.
News of Smaug's death reaches Gandalf, Beorn, and the Goblins.
The Elvenking's host marches out of Mirkwood, bound for the wealth of Erebor.
The Elven host turns south to aid Lake-town.
The Gathering of the Clouds. The Elves reach Lake-town; Dáin is summoned from the Iron Hills.
The Elves and Lake-men arrive at Dale as night falls.
Parley fails. The Lonely Mountain is besieged.
A Thief in the Night. Bilbo secretly brings the Arkenstone to Bard and the Elvenking, hoping to prevent war.
Dáin arrives. The Clouds Burst. Goblins and Wargs attack. The Battle of Five Armies.
There and Back Again. Gandalf and Bilbo depart the Lonely Mountain with Beorn.
Gandalf and Bilbo spend the winter at Beorn's.
Bilbo goes home with mithril, gold, and the Ring. Sauron secretly returns to Mordor.
King Bard rebuilds Dale. Gollum leaves the Mountains, hunting for his Precious.
Théoden is born.
Gandalf and Balin visit Bilbo in the Shire. 'You are a very fine person, Mr. Baggins, and I am very fond of you; but you are only quite a little fellow in a wide world after all!'
Finduilas, mother of Boromir and Faramir, is born.
Sauron openly declares himself, rebuilds Barad-dûr. Gollum heads toward Mordor. Aragorn learns of his ancestry from Elrond, meets Arwen.
Last meeting of the White Council. Saruman lies, claiming the One Ring swept out to Sea. He fortifies Isengard and, jealous of Gandalf, spies on the Shire.
Mount Doom re-awakens in fire and ash. Anyone left in Ithilien flees.
Aragorn meets Gandalf for the first time.
Aragorn's secret years begin. In the following decades, he serves Rohan and Gondor in disguise, and journeys in Rhûn and Harad, even into the borderlands of Mordor.
Frodo is born.
Denethor marries Finduilas of Dol Amroth.
Death of Bard. Bain, his son, becomes King.
Boromir is born.
Birth of Samwise Gamgee. Aragorn and Arwen betrothed upon Cerin Amroth in Lórien. Théoden becomes King of Rohan. Gollum meets Shelob.
Birth of Meriadoc Brandybuck.
Faramir is born.
Denethor II becomes Steward of Gondor, and steward of a palantír.
Finduilas, mother of Boromir and Faramir, dies young.
Against advice, Balin re-establishes the dwarf colony in Khazad-dûm.
Birth of Peregrin Took.
Éomer is born.
Balin slain; no dwarf in Moria survives to tell the tale.
Éowyn, sister of Éomer, is born.
Saruman turns traitor after using the palantír of Orthanc and falling under Sauron's influence.

The Long-Expected Party. Bilbo disappears in front of the entire Shire. Bilbo begrudgingly but voluntarily leaves the Ring to Frodo. Gandalf suspects Bilbo's ring; he and Aragorn hunt for Gollum. The guard on the Shire is doubled.
Bilbo settles in Imladris and begins his Translations from the Elvish.
Gandalf regularly visits Frodo for the next four years.
Brand, grandson of Bard, becomes King in Dale.
Gandalf's last visit to Frodo for many years.

Over the next eight years, Gandalf and Aragorn redouble their hunt for Gollum. At some point, Gollum is captured inside Mordor and taken to Barad-dûr. Arwen returns to Rivendell; travel is becoming dangerous.

Deliberately released from Mordor, Gollum is captured by Aragorn in the Dead Marshes and brought to the Wood-elves in Mirkwood. Gandalf reads the scroll of Isildur in the archives of Minas Tirith. A servant of Sauron arrives in Dale, seeking news of hobbits.
The Shadow of the Past. Gandalf and Frodo throw Bilbo's ring into the fire and read its inscription. The War of the Ring begins.
Gandalf tells Aragorn of Frodo's plan to leave the Shire in September.
Sauron attacks Osgiliath; the Nazgûl cross the river, hunting hobbits. Gollum escapes from the Wood-elves during a similar attack.
Saruman tricks Radagast into sending Gandalf to Orthanc with news that the Nazgûl have crossed the Anduin seeking the Shire. Gandalf leaves a letter for Frodo.
Boromir sets out from Minas Tirith after he and Faramir receive a prophetic dream.
Gandalf comes to Saruman for help and ends up imprisoned on the top of Orthanc.
All trace of Gollum is lost. Hunted by Elves and Sauron, he hides in Moria and cannot get out.
The Eagle Gwaihir, sent by Radagast with news, rescues Gandalf. The Black Riders cross the Fords of Isen under new orders from Sauron.
Disguised as a beggar, Gandalf is refused entry to Edoras.
Gandalf gains an audience with the King; Théoden commands him to take any horse and leave within a day. The Black Riders come to Isengard; Saruman deceives them.
Gandalf meets Shadowfax and spends two days taming him. The Black Riders meet Grima Wormtongue, who reveals the location of the Shire and the full extent of Saruman's treachery.
The Black Riders overwhelm the Ranger guard on the Shire's southern border. Frodo turns 50.
Four Black Riders enter the Shire before dawn; one reaches Hobbiton at nightfall, narrowly missing Frodo as he leaves Bag End.
Passing High Elves scare off a Black Rider and shelter the hobbits for the night.
Farmer Maggot gives the hobbits a ride to Bucklebury Ferry after encountering a Black Rider.
The hobbits enter the Old Forest. Tom Bombadil rescues them from Old Man Willow.
The hobbits spend a second night with Bombadil.
Captured by a Barrow-wight, the hobbits are again rescued by Bombadil. Merry picks up a blade that could kill a Witch-king
The hobbits meet Strider at the Prancing Pony.
Black Riders wreck the inn in the early hours. The hobbits and Strider leave later that morning.
Frodo sees distant flashes in the night; Gandalf fights the Nazgûl on Weathertop.
Black Riders attack. Frodo is stabbed by the Witch-king's Morgul blade.
Frodo rides a pony, gradually worsening.
Glorfindel comes upon three Nazgûl. 'They withdrew and I pursued them.' He leaves a token of safety.
Finding a token of safety, the Company crosses the Bridge. Frodo worsens, becoming a wraith.
They stumble upon Bilbo's trolls. Glorfindel (Arwen in the movie) finds them at dusk.
Flight to the Ford. Frodo rides Glorfindel's horse.
Frodo, alone and dying, defies the Nazgûl. The Ringwraiths pause; the flood sweeps them away.
Frodo wakes to Gandalf at his side.
The Council of Elrond. Luckily, precisely the right people are in Rivendell on separate errands at the same time.
Autumn wanes and December passes. Preparations are made, scouts sent, people consulted.
The Fellowship of the Ring is formed. Elrond, sensing the hand of Providence, goes with the stupid plan: send Merry and Pippin.
The Fellowship departs Rivendell.
The Ring Goes South.
The Fellowship cross into Hollin. Spooked by crebain, they spend the day in hiding.
The Fellowship attempts the Redhorn Pass. Snow and bitter cold drive them back.
Wolves attack in the night. The bodies vanish by morning.
Speak 'friend' and enter. The Fellowship enters Moria. Gollum begins to trail the Ring-Bearer.
A Journey in the Dark.
The Bridge of Khazad-dûm, and fall of Gandalf.
Elves escort the blindfolded Fellowship into Lothlórien.
Galdriel and Celeborn welcome the Fellowship in Caras Galadhon.
The Fellowship rests and heals in Lórien, grieving for Gandalf.
Gandalf pursues the Balrog to the peak of Zirak-zigil.
Gandalf slays the Balrog, and dies. As do all who kill a Balrog.
The Fellowship recovers in Lothlórien.
The Mirror of Galadriel. Frodo offers her the Ring, which she refuses. Gandalf returns to life.
Farewell to Lórien. Gollum follows.
The Fellowship floats down the Great River. Boats: far quicker than walking.
Orc archers ambush the Fellowship in the night. Legolas shoots down the winged steed of a Nazgûl.
The Fellowship passes between the Argonath and camps at Parth Galen, not knowing which path to take next.
Breaking of the Fellowship. Boromir tries to take the Ring. Frodo and Sam head east alone.
Breaking of the Fellowship. Boromir slain defending Merry and Pippin; Orcs take them. Aragorn sets out in pursuit.
Frodo and Sam are lost in the barren slopes and stones of the Emyn Muil.
The Three Hunters race across the plains of Rohan.
The Taming of Sméagol. Frodo and Sam capture Gollum. He leads them out of the Emyn Muil.
The Three Hunters meet the Riders of Rohan and learn of the Orcs' destruction. Éomer lends them horses.
Gollum leads Frodo and Sam into the Dead Marshes.
Aragorn meets Gandalf the White in Fangorn. They ride for Edoras.
Frodo and Sam reach the far edge of the Dead Marshes.
Gandalf heals Théoden; the Rohirrim ride to war.
The Battle of the Hornburg. No elves are present, although it's great in the movie.
Frodo comes to the Desolation of the Morannon.
Victorious, Théoden and Gandalf set out from Helm's Deep for Isengard.
The Black Gate is closed. Gollum leads them south.
Parley with Saruman in Orthanc. Pippin looks into the palantír. A Nazgûl flies over the camp. Gandalf and Pippin ride for Minas Tirith.
Of Herbs and Stewed Rabbit.
Aragorn reveals himself to Sauron in the palantír. Théoden rides for Dunharrow; Aragorn follows with the Grey Company.
Frodo and Sam taken by the Rangers of Ithilien. Faramir immediately refuses the Ring, unlike the movie.
Aragorn comes to Dunharrow at nightfall. Gandalf and Pippin see the beacon-light of Gondor.
Frodo leaves Henneth Annûn. Gollum feels betrayed at the Forbidden Pool.
Aragorn takes the Paths of the Dead at daybreak. He summons the Dead Men of Dunharrow to fulfill their 3,000-year-old oath.
Frodo reaches the Morgul-road at dusk.
Gandalf and Pippin arrive at Minas Tirith. Darkness begins to flow out of Mordor.
The Dawnless Day. Frodo sees the army of Minas Morgul march forth.
The Dawnless Day. The Muster of Rohan. Gandalf rescues Faramir outside the gates of Minas Tirith.
Gollum visits Shelob. He nearly repents over a sleeping Frodo, but Sam ruins it.
Denethor orders Faramir to defend Osgiliath.
Gollum leads Frodo and Sam into Shelob's Lair.
Aragorn drives the enemy south toward Pelargir. Faramir retreats to the Causeway Forts.
Shelob stings Frodo and is in turn wounded by Sam. Sam takes the Ring. Orcs take Frodo. The Choices of Master Samwise.
The Pelennor is overrun. Faramir is wounded; Denethor breaks. Aragorn captures the Corsair fleet at Pelargir and releases the Dead.
Sam finds Frodo alive in the Tower.
Minas Tirith is besieged. Théoden takes a shortcut.
Frodo and Sam escape and begin their journey north along the Morgai. Sam sees a star.

At dawn, the Witch-king breaks the gates of the City. The horns of Rohan sound. Battle of the Pelennor Fields. Denethor burns, Théoden falls, and the Witch-king is destroyed. Aragorn arrives with the fleet to save the City.
Frodo looks out over the armies of Mordor towards Mount Doom.
The Last Debate. The commanders arrange a diversionary assault on the Black Gate, drawing Sauron's gaze from Frodo.
The Land of Shadow.
The Host of the West musters.
Frodo and Sam are caught up in an Orc march through Mordor and slip away the following day.
The Host of the West marches out from Minas Tirith.
The Land of Shadow.
The Host of the West marches through Ithilien.
Frodo and Sam turn south towards Mount Doom.
Frodo and Sam cast away their gear.
Aragorn dismisses the faint-hearted, sending them to free Cair Andros.
Frodo and Sam reach the feet of Mount Doom.
The Host camps in the Desolation of the Morannon.
Sam carries Frodo uphill. Frodo fails; Gollum bites the Ring off his hand and falls into the Cracks of Doom. Sauron is ended.
The Black Gate is open. The Host is surrounded. Eucatastrophe. The Ring is destroyed and Sauron passes away.
